extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in peer review, mechanism design, and machine learning (conference organizers, program committees, ML/CS researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Design and analysis of the Isotonic Mechanism: a method that combines owner-provided ranking with noisy reviewer scores to produce adjusted item scores that are computationally efficient and incentive-aligned. The work proves conditions under which the owner is incentivized to report truthfully and shows accuracy improvements over raw reviewer scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isotonic Mechanism — inputs and outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: This mechanism takes as input the ranking of the items from best to worst provided by the owner, in addition to the raw scores provided by the reviewers. It reports adjusted scores for the items by solving a convex optimization problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverages owner-provided ranking along with reviewer scores to produce adjusted scores; the mechanism is framed as an isotonic regression/convex optimization procedure. Use of both inputs is central to operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Owner incentive to report truthfully (incentive compatibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under certain conditions, the owner's optimal strategy is to honestly report the true ranking of the items to her best knowledge in order to maximize the expected utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper provides conditions and proofs showing that, given the mechanism, an owner maximizes expected utility by reporting an honest ranking; mechanism design ensures the owner is incentivized to provide the ranking rather than withhold it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improved accuracy relative to raw reviewer scores
rubrics_metrics.description: The adjusted scores provided by this owner-assisted mechanism are indeed significantly more accurate than the raw scores provided by the reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The claim is supported by theoretical results in the paper (and presumably experiments in the poster/supplement); the mechanism should yield measurable accuracy improvements (e.g., lower estimation error) compared to using noisy reviewer scores alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addresses owner withholding of information
rubrics_metrics.description: The mechanism is designed for the setting where the owner of items knows the true underlying scores but prefers not to provide this information; it addresses this withholding by leveraging information the owner is incentivized to provide (a ranking).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes real-world tendency of owners to withhold detailed information; instead elicits ranking (less direct than scores) because owners are more willing to provide or can be incentivized to provide it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computational simplicity and efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: The Isotonic Mechanism is described as a simple and efficient approach that reports adjusted scores by solving a convex optimization problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convex optimization formulation implies computational tractability and practical implementability; the poster emphasizes simplicity and efficiency as desirable properties.
